Commentary.Commentary: So, what will be the Sri Lankan's intentions as they come out to bat? Will they want to attack and make up for some lost time as Zimbabwe have batted for almost two days or will they start slow and then grow into the game. Oshada Fernando and Dimuth Karunaratne are stepping out to answer all your questions with Kyle Jarvis bowling first up to them!

The Lankans toiled for 2 long hard days in the field but finally got the reward for their patience. Embuldeniya was the star with the ball for Sri Lanka as he picked up a 5-fer. Suranga Lakmal and Lahiru Kumara also chipped in with 3 and 2 wickets each. They will not be mightily pleased with how long it has taken them to dismiss the Zimbabwe batters but will make do with what they have now.

The innings started superbly for the hosts as they managed to stitch a 96-run opening stand before  Prince Masvaure departed after making his half ton. Kevin Kasuza then combined with Craig Ervine to form a 50-plus run stand with the former completing his half ton along the way. Zimbabwe were cruising along until Sean Williams and Brendon Taylor were at the crease but after that their innings started to fall apart bit by bit. In the back end of the innings, Sikandar Raza and Donald Tiripano added valuable runs to the total and guided the hosts to a total of 358 runs. Craig Ervine though was the pick of the batters as he scored 85 runs showing his class.

Sri Lanka have taken a long time to wrap up the Zimbabwe innings due to the 10th-wicket partnership but they have eventually found a way and their bowlers will now be hoping for a long rest after almost 2 days of extremely hard work in the field.

Alright then, it has been a session which has passed by slowly but has been dominated by Sri Lanka. They have picked up four wickets in this session and the bowlers have done well to keep it tight. Lasith Embuldeniya picked up a five-wicket haul and has bowled really well. On the other hand, for the hosts, Sikandar Raza played a handy innings and ensured Zimbabwe cross the 300-run mark. Donald Tiripano has also played well and is right now unbeaten on 41 runs, trying to swell the score as much as he can before they lose their last wicket. When the 9th wicket fell, the session was extended by a further 30 minutes but that did not help the Lankans as they could not manage to take the last wicket. Tiripano and Victor Nyauchi have done well to grind out the latter part of this session. Tiripano has faced close to a 100 balls and has done well to not throw away his wicket. Join us back in a bit to find out what will happen in the last session of the day as Zimbabwe hold on to their last wicket and the Lankans toil hard on the field.

Overs - 26, Runs - 71, Wickets - 3! This was the story of the morning session. It once again started on the slower side and it appeared that once again the visiting team is in for a big toil. Post that, yet another partnership prospered but at the stroke of Lunch, Sri Lanka managed to pick two wickets in two overs, which included Craig Ervine, and that handed the session to the Islanders. Considering that it's a very flat pitch, the hosts would be hoping that the remaining batsmen contribute well and take their first innings' total close to 350, if not more. Let's see what happens next in the afternoon session. Do join us in a short while for all the action.

A warm welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe in Harare. It was a very slow day of Test cricket, a typical one, reminding us of the old days when the batsmen used to grind themselves out and concentrate more on preserving wickets than scoring runs. In this modern era of Twenty20 cricket, that may sound like boring but this is what the Test cricket originally was all about. Agreed that the approach of the teams has changed nowadays but for a team like Zimbabwe which is trying to re-establish themselves alongside the big boys, we can understand that they want to take things cautiously. Having said all that, the onus also falls on Sri Lanka, who are supposed to be a better team, to pick wickets which they failed to do. That brings the pitch into picture which wears a flat look at the moment but is expected to break in the coming days. Will the African minnow up their scoring rate today and get a substantial first innings total? Or are we going to see the Lankan Lions roar back to show what they got? We are not too far away from the first ball...
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

That's all from Day 1 of this Test match. Zimbabwe have had a terrific day in the field and they will look to get as many runs as possible on Day 2 and put further pressure on the Lankans. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, would be disappointed but they are not entirely out of it. They need to pick up quick wickets though and get Zimbabwe out for a cheap score. What will happen on Day 2? Will the Lankan Lions roar back or will Zimbabwe run away with the game. Join us on Monday, the 20th of January at 1000 Local (0800 GMT) for another engrossing day of Test match cricket. Until then, good night.

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, bowled their hearts out. They kept on bowling tight lines and lengths but were unable to reap the reward. Lasith Embuldeniya picked up one wicket while Kumara was lucky to get his wicket off a full toss. Suranga Lakmal and Kasun Rajitha too bowled well but the Zimbabwean batters played everything solidly which came their way. Overall, a tough day in the field for the visitors.

Unfortunately, it has been called Stumps on Day 1 with only 6 overs remaining in the day's play. A day that has belonged to Zimbabwe. They started brilliantly with a 96-run stand between Prince Masvoure and Kevin Kasuza. Both reached their respective fifties. Although they were a little slow but they laid a solid foundation for the rest of the batters. They lost Masvoure soon after Lunch but Craig Ervine came out and adopted a positive approach and got to his half ton as well. Kevin Kasuza looked set for a ton but missed out on a full toss as he fell. Since then, Taylor and Ervine managed to play out the remaining overs before bad light stopped play. Their run rate might be a little on the slower side but will be happy going into Day 2.
